sourceFacts.fact: Bacteria can enter via the urethra and infect the bladder.
Infection can spread upwards via ureters to one or both kidneys.
Ascending spread is possible rather than inevitable.

labels: A common route of urinary infection
layout: A vertical staircase of FOUR disconnected paper labels, beginning at lower left node1 and ascending diagonally to upper right node4. Three broad arrows point UP the staircase. Show neutral purple bead tokens traveling along these PAGE arrows, no bacterial morphology. Use small sublabel Cystitis under2 and Pyelonephritis under4. Caption: Infection may ascend; progression is not inevitable. Absolutely no urethral tube, bladder outline, ureters, kidneys or human body; this is a logical sequence with site names only.
